text: You just sliced into an onion, and now you're crying like you watched a sad movie.
An onion is packed with millions of tiny cells, like water balloons.
Your knife smashes them open, and two things inside mix that were kept apart.
Special helpers called enzymes grab the onion's sulfur and change it fast.
In seconds, it turns into a sneaky gas that floats straight up.
It's the onion's alarm, made to scare off hungry animals.
The gas drifts right into your eyes and mixes with the wet layer on top.
That makes a tiny bit of acid, and your eyes start to sting.
So your tear glands open the floodgates to wash it all away.
Want fewer tears? Chill the onion first, because cold slows the reaction way down.
Or cut it near a fan to blow the gas away.
Subscribe, because that's why onions make you cry.
